stem: Oligoarticular arthritis is classified by the involvement of how many joints during the first six months of disease?

options.text: Only the small joints of the hands

explanation: Oligoarticular arthritis is defined as affecting four or fewer joints, typically large joints of the lower limbs.
rationale: The prefix 'oligo-' suggests 'few,' placing the limit just below five.

optionExplanations.A: Oligoarticular arthritis is defined as affecting four or fewer joints, typically large joints of the lower limbs.
optionExplanations.B: Five or more joints would classify the condition as polyarticular arthritis.
optionExplanations.C: While it can affect one joint (monoarthritis), the classification allows for up to four joints.
optionExplanations.D: Oligoarticular arthritis typically affects large joints, whereas polyarticular arthritis more often involves small joints.

source.hint: The prefix 'oligo-' suggests 'few,' placing the limit just below five.
